questions.text: Write x² + 8x – 5 in the form (x + p)² – q.
questions.markingGuide: Completing the square: x² + 8x – 5. Half of 8 is 4, so (x + 4)² = x² + 8x + 16. Therefore x² + 8x – 5 = (x + 4)² – 16 – 5 = (x + 4)² – 21. Achieved: Expression correctly written in the form (x + 4)² – 21.

questions.text: Find the discriminant of the quadratic equation 3x² + 2 = 5x.
questions.markingGuide: First rearrange to standard form: 3x² – 5x + 2 = 0. Here a = 3, b = –5, c = 2. Discriminant = b² – 4ac = (–5)² – 4(3)(2) = 25 – 24 = 1. Achieved: Correct discriminant value of 1. Note: Students must rearrange to standard form first — using a = 3, b = 5, c = 2 (without the negative on b) still gives 25 – 24 = 1, but using the equation in its original form (e.g. a = 3, b = –5, c = –2) gives an incorrect answer of 49.

questions.text:
Write as a single fraction in its simplest form:

1/t + (t – 5)/(3t²) – 1/t
questions.markingGuide: Note that 1/t – 1/t = 0, so the expression simplifies to (t – 5)/(3t²). Alternatively, using common denominator 3t²: 1/t = 3t/(3t²), so 3t/(3t²) + (t – 5)/(3t²) – 3t/(3t²) = (3t + t – 5 – 3t)/(3t²) = (t – 5)/(3t²). Achieved: Puts at least two fractions over a common denominator and simplifies the numerator. Merit: Fully simplified single fraction (t – 5)/(3t²).

questions.text:
A cubic polynomial f(x) = 3x³ + ax² + bx + c has roots –2, 1/3, and 4.

Find the values of the constants a, b, and c.
questions.markingGuide: Since the roots are –2, 1/3, and 4, and the leading coefficient is 3: f(x) = 3(x + 2)(x – 1/3)(x – 4). Alternatively: f(x) = (x + 2)(3x – 1)(x – 4). Expanding (x + 2)(3x – 1) = 3x² – x + 6x – 2 = 3x² + 5x – 2. Then (3x² + 5x – 2)(x – 4) = 3x³ + 5x² – 2x – 12x² – 20x + 8 = 3x³ – 7x² – 22x + 8. So a = –7, b = –22, c = 8. Alternative method: substitute each root into f(x) = 0 to get three simultaneous equations, then solve. f(–2) = 0: –24 + 4a – 2b + c = 0. f(1/3) = 0: 1/9 + a/9 + b/3 + c = 0. f(4) = 0: 192 + 16a + 4b + c = 0. Achieved: Identifies the three correct factors (x + 2), (3x – 1), and (x – 4), OR correctly substitutes a root to form an equation in a, b, c. Merit: Correctly finds all three values a = –7, b = –22, c = 8.

Numerator: (x^(3/2) + x^(–1/2))(x^(1/2) – x^(–1/2)). Expand using FOIL: x^(3/2)·x^(1/2) – x^(3/2)·x^(–1/2) + x^(–1/2)·x^(1/2) – x^(–1/2)·x^(–1/2) = x² – x + 1 – x^(–1) = x² – x + 1 – 1/x. Alternatively, factor out from numerator terms: x^(–1/2)(x² + 1) · x^(–1/2)(x – 1) = x^(–1)(x² + 1)(x – 1). Denominator: (x^(3/2) – x^(1/2))² = [x^(1/2)(x – 1)]² = x(x – 1)². Full simplification: Numerator = x^(–1)(x² + 1)(x – 1) = (x² + 1)(x – 1)/x. Wait — recheck: x^(3/2) + x^(–1/2) = x^(–1/2)(x² + 1). x^(1/2) – x^(–1/2) = x^(–1/2)(x – 1). So numerator = x^(–1)(x² + 1)(x – 1). Denominator = x(x – 1)². Result = (x² + 1)(x – 1) / [x · x(x – 1)²] = (x² + 1) / [x²(x – 1)]. Hmm — this doesn't match the target. Alternative expansion: check if the original expression uses x^(3/2) + x^(1/2) in first bracket. If numerator factors are (x^(1/2)(x + 1)) and (x^(–1/2)(x – 1)), numerator = (x + 1)(x – 1). Denominator = x(x – 1)². Result = (x + 1)(x – 1)/[x(x – 1)²] = (x + 1)/[x(x – 1)]. Achieved: Correct expansion of either the numerator or the denominator. Merit: Correct factorisation of either the expanded numerator or denominator. Excellence (t1): Derives the result but with minor incorrect mathematical statements (e.g. missing steps or sign errors that self-correct). Excellence (t2): Mathematically rigorous and correct proof throughout.

Multiply both sides by x: 3x² – 14x = 5. Rearrange: 3x² – 14x – 5 = 0. Factorise: (3x + 1)(x – 5) = 0. So x = –1/3 or x = 5. Alternatively, use the quadratic formula: x = [14 ± √(196 + 60)] / 6 = [14 ± √256] / 6 = [14 ± 16] / 6. x = 30/6 = 5 or x = –2/6 = –1/3. Achieved: Both solutions x = –1/3 and x = 5 found correctly.

Numerator: 9x² + 30x + 25 = (3x + 5)². Denominator: 5x + 3x² = x(5 + 3x) = x(3x + 5). So the expression = (3x + 5)² / [x(3x + 5)] = (3x + 5) / x. Achieved: Correctly factorising the numerator as (3x + 5)² OR the denominator as x(3x + 5). Merit: Fully simplified result (3x + 5) / x.

questions.text:
Find the value of k for which the equation

(x² – 2x) / (4x – 1) = (k – 1) / (k + 1)

has roots that are numerically equal but opposite in sign.
questions.markingGuide: Cross-multiply: (x² – 2x)(k + 1) = (k – 1)(4x – 1). Expand LHS: (k + 1)x² – 2(k + 1)x. Expand RHS: 4(k – 1)x – (k – 1). Rearrange: (k + 1)x² – 2(k + 1)x – 4(k – 1)x + (k – 1) = 0. (k + 1)x² – [2(k + 1) + 4(k – 1)]x + (k – 1) = 0. (k + 1)x² – (2k + 2 + 4k – 4)x + (k – 1) = 0. (k + 1)x² – (6k – 2)x + (k – 1) = 0. For roots numerically equal but opposite in sign (i.e. roots are r and –r), the sum of roots = 0. Sum of roots = (6k – 2) / (k + 1) = 0. So 6k – 2 = 0, giving k = 1/3. Achieved: Correctly cross-multiplying and expanding to remove denominators. Merit: Fully expanded and simplified quadratic in x with coefficients in terms of k. Excellence: Correct value k = 1/3, using the condition that equal-and-opposite roots means the sum of roots is zero.

questions.text:
The logo for an IT company, Doctor of Data, is shown in the diagram. The green background of the logo is the shape of a rectangle with length x. The letters D, O, D are formed using semi-circles for both Ds and a circle for the O. Each has the same radius.

Find an expression in terms of x for the area of the circle in the middle of the logo (i.e. the letter 'O').
questions.markingGuide: The rectangle contains two semicircles (the two D's) and one full circle (the O). Two semicircles = one full circle, so effectively two full circles span the length. Each circle has diameter 2r, and the length x = 2 × (2r) = 4r. So r = x/4. Height of rectangle = 2r = x/2. Area of one circle = πr² = π(x/4)² = πx²/16. Achieved: Correct expression πx²/16, or a correct relationship between r and x (r = x/4).

questions.text: If the green background has an area of 10 cm², find the length of the rectangle.
questions.markingGuide: Rectangle area = x × (x/2) = x²/2. Letter area = two semicircles + one circle = two full circles = 2πr² = 2π(x/4)² = 2πx²/16 = πx²/8. Green area = Rectangle – Letters = x²/2 – πx²/8 = x²(1/2 – π/8) = x²(4 – π)/8. Setting equal to 10: x²(4 – π)/8 = 10. x² = 80/(4 – π) = 80/0.8584 = 93.20. x = √93.20 = 9.65 cm. Achieved: Correct expression for the green area in terms of x or r. Merit: Correct value for the length x = 9.65 cm (accept 9.7 cm to 1 d.p.).

Convert to base 3: 9 = 3², so 9^(2x + 3) = 3^(2(2x + 3)) = 3^(4x + 6). 1/27 = 3^(–3), so (1/27)^x = 3^(–3x). Setting exponents equal: 4x + 6 = –3x. 7x = –6. x = –6/7. Achieved: Correctly converts both sides to the same base (base 3). Merit: Correct solution x = –6/7 with working shown.

questions.text: If log_b x = 2 and log_(3b) y = 2, write y in terms of x.
questions.markingGuide: From log_b x = 2: b² = x, so b = √x = x^(1/2). From log_(3b) y = 2: (3b)² = y, so y = 9b². Since b² = x: y = 9x. Achieved: Correctly converting one logarithmic equation to exponential form (e.g. b² = x or (3b)² = y). Merit: Converting both equations and establishing a relationship between them. Excellence: Correct answer y = 9x with clear logical working.

questions.text:
Consider the quadratic equation 3x² – 4kx + k² = 0.

Using the quadratic formula, find fully simplified solutions for x in terms of k.
questions.markingGuide: Using the quadratic formula with a = 3, b = –4k, c = k²: x = [–(–4k) ± √((–4k)² – 4(3)(k²))] / (2 × 3). x = [4k ± √(16k² – 12k²)] / 6. x = [4k ± √(4k²)] / 6. x = [4k ± 2k] / 6. So x = (4k + 2k)/6 = 6k/6 = k, or x = (4k – 2k)/6 = 2k/6 = k/3. Achieved: Correctly substitutes a = 3, b = –4k, c = k² into the quadratic formula. Merit: Fully simplified solutions x = k and x = k/3.
